## The Global Shark Attack File

The Global Shark Attack File (GSAF) is a historical archive compiled by researchers to document human-shark interactions from coastal waters across the world. Spanning more than a century of incident logs, physician case reports, and verified media records, it provides empirical evidence on where, when, and under what conditions encounters happen.

## Perception vs. Reality

Sensational media headlines and movies often portray sharks as relentless hunters, fueling a level of public anxiety far beyond the actual statistical risk. In reality, the odds of experiencing a shark attack are vanishingly small. Ocean-goers face vastly greater dangers from rip currents, boat collisions, and accidental drowning than from wildlife. Furthermore, when encounters do happen, the vast majority are non-fatal—most often representing exploratory curiosity or mistaken identity rather than targeted aggression.
